subject: Life Skills
title: Normalcy Bias
description: A short lesson to help you apply Normalcy Bias.

hook.text: When the Titanic hit the iceberg, many passengers stayed in the dining room for another hour. They could not believe it.

buildup.text: Normalcy bias makes your brain reject evidence that something abnormal is happening. 'It is probably fine' on repeat.

discovery.text: Studies show up to 70% of people freeze or deny during the first minutes of an emergency. Only a few act immediately.

twist.text: The bias is strongest when the event has never happened to you before. Your brain has no script for it.

climax.text: Fight it by pre-scripting: when you enter a plane, locate two exits. When a fire alarm rings, leave. No thinking needed.

punchline.text: When alarms ring, move first and analyze later.

quiz.question: What does normalcy bias cause people to do in emergencies?
options: Deny the danger and delay action
Seek out the source of danger
